x: Over the first small lap Peter Curry, the Olympic Games steeplechase representative was in the lead closely followed by Derrick Burfitt. On completion of the first big lap, Curry and Burfitt had drawn away from the rest of the field and were running stride for stride.

Our team got away to a good start and quickly showed to advantage with Derrick Burfitt and Vern Blowfield among the leaders. Derrick and Olney (T.V.H.) soon sorted themselves out and together fighting all the way Olney eventually won on the tape by taking the "proverbial deep breath," the timekeeper…
In the mile Marchant qualified in 4.31 and Burfitt in 4 mins 33 secs. In the final Burfitt was fourth and Marchant sixth.

Bishop. 1 mile (under 19).—Musselbrook Cup: 1st, M. Stearman, 2nd, Hazell; 3rd, Maclean, 4 mins. 48 secs. 1 mile.—Garnett Cup: 1st, Burfitt; 2nd, Brown; 3rd, W.

The course was a sticky one of 7½ miles and Derrick Burfitt was first man home followed by Ted Stimpson. Vern Blowfield had an easy run in fourth position and it looks as if these three will form the spearhead of our team for the coming cross-country championships.

The other members finished as follows:—Charlton 16th, Tobin 33rd, Ken Stimpson 45th, MacDonald 59th, Heard 68th and Housego 127th. The team finished fifth, quite a good performance without such stars as Burfitt, Blowfield and Smart.

Going back that far reminds me of that exceptional performance in 1945 when with Burfitt (1), Main (2), Pearson (3) and Eeles (13) Belgrave 'A' won with 19 points, to be followed by Tobin (5), Clinton (7), Smart (17) and Jarlett (26) who brought home Belgrave 'B' in second place.
